nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}^d$ be a set of cells and let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. Then $A$ contains $P$ when there are maps $f_1, \dots, f_d : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that each $f_i$ is strictly increasing on the set $\{p_i : p \in P\}$ of $i$-th coordinates of points of $P$, and $(f_1(p_1), \dots, f_d(p_d)) \in A$ for every $p \in P$.
nodes.title: Containment of a point pattern in d-dimensional grid cells

nodes.summary: A set of cells $A \subseteq \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, each cell written (column, row), contains a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ when there are maps $f_X, f_Y : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $f_X$ is strictly increasing on the set of $x$-coordinates of points of $P$, $f_Y$ is strictly increasing on the set of $y$-coordinates of points of $P$, and $(f_X(x), f_Y(y)) \in A$ for every $(x, y) \in P$.
nodes.title: Containment of a point pattern in a set of grid cells

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d$ and every set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $S$ contains the empty set $\emptyset \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ in the sense of containment of point sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.title: Every set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains the empty pattern

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number and let $S, P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. Then $S$ contains $P$ when there are maps $f_1, \dots, f_d : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that expand distances between coordinates of points of $P$, that is, $f_i(p_i) - f_i(q_i) \ge p_i - q_i$ for every $i$ and all $p, q \in P$ with $p_i > q_i$, and such that $(f_1(p_1), \dots, f_d(p_d)) \in S$ for every $p \in P$.
nodes.title: Containment of point sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$ there is a set $S$ of cells of the $n \times n$ grid $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}^2$ with $|S| \ge \frac{1}{2} n^{2 - 2/(r+1)}$ that contains no $r \times r$ all-ones submatrix: there are no sets $R, C \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with $|R| = |C| = r$ and $R \times C \subseteq S$.
nodes.title: Large sets of grid cells with no $r \times r$ all-ones submatrix

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number and let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be finite. Then there is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the $d$-dimensional continuous Turán number satisfies $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) = O(n^{d - \varepsilon})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Power saving for continuous Turán numbers of finite patterns in $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set whose points have pairwise distinct $y$-coordinates. Then there is a natural number $t$ such that $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n \cdot 2^{\alpha(n)^t})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity, where $\operatorname{opx}$ is the continuous Turán number and $\alpha$ is the inverse Ackermann function.
nodes.title: Almost linear bound for patterns with at most one point in each row

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be finite. Then there is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the continuous Turán number satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n^{2 - \varepsilon})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Power saving for continuous Turán numbers of finite planar patterns

nodes.summary: The inverse Ackermann function $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha(8) = 3$, since $A(2, 2) = 7 < 8 \le 61 = A(3, 3)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.
nodes.title: The inverse Ackermann function at 8

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, if $n \le A(k, k)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function, then $\alpha(n) \le k$, where $\alpha$ is the inverse Ackermann function.
nodes.title: Upper bound for the inverse Ackermann function

nodes.summary: The inverse Ackermann function $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha(2) = 1$, since $A(0, 0) = 1 < 2 \le 3 = A(1, 1)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.
nodes.title: The inverse Ackermann function at 2

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the inverse Ackermann function $\alpha(n)$ is the least natural number $k$ with $n \le A(k, k)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function, given for all natural numbers $m$ and $j$ by $A(0, j) = j + 1$, $A(m + 1, 0) = A(m, 1)$ and $A(m + 1, j + 1) = A(m, A(m + 1, j))$.
nodes.title: Inverse Ackermann function

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a real number and let $P$ and $S$ be subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$. Then $S$ is saturating for $P$ in $[0, n]^2$ when $S$ is an open subset of $[0, n]^2$ that does not contain $P$, while every open set $S'$ with $S \subsetneq S' \subseteq [0, n]^2$ contains $P$. Here a set $T$ contains $P$ when there are maps $f_X, f_Y : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f_X(x) - f_X(x') \ge x - x'$ whenever $x > x'$ are…
nodes.title: Saturating sets for a point pattern

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, $n \le A(\alpha(n), \alpha(n))$, where $\alpha$ is the inverse Ackermann function and $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.
nodes.title: Defining inequality of the inverse Ackermann function

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, $n$ a real number and $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, and let $\Pr(P)$ be the subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ obtained by dropping the last coordinate of every point of $P$. Writing $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q, k)$ for the $k$-dimensional continuous Turán number, we have $n \cdot \mathrm{opx}(n, \Pr(P), d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n, P, d + 1)$.
nodes.title: Projection bound for the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $n, \delta$ be real numbers with $n > 0$ and $0 < \delta < n$. Then the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}$ satisfies $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) \le \mathrm{opx}(n + \delta, P)$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n + \delta, P) < \mathrm{opx}(n, P) + 3 n \delta$.
nodes.title: Increment bound for the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For every $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P)$ is a continuous function of $n$ on $(0, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, and let $n, \varepsilon$ be real numbers with $n > 0$ and $0 < \varepsilon < n$. Then the $d$-dimensional continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}$ satisfies $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n + \varepsilon, P, d)$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n + \varepsilon, P, d) < \mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) + d (2n)^{d-1} \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Increment bound for the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d$ and every $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, the $d$-dimensional continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d)$ is a continuous function of $n$ on $(0, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be finite and let $c_1, c_2, q, n$ be real numbers with $c_1 > 0$, $q > 1$ and $n > 0$. Suppose that for every coordinate $i$ and all $p, p' \in P$ with $p_i < p'_i$ such that no $r \in P$ has $p_i < r_i < p'_i$, we have $c_1 \le p'_i - p_i \le c_2$. Let $qP = \{q p : p \in P\}$ and $m = \lceil q c_2 / c_1 \rceil + 1$. Then the $d$-dimensional continuous…
nodes.title: Dilation bound for the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For every dimension $d$ and every real number $n$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, \emptyset, d) = 0$: every set contains the empty pattern, so no set is free of it.
nodes.title: The higher-dimensional continuous Turán number of the empty pattern

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ be a set whose points all have the same last coordinate, and let $\mathrm{Pr}(P) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be the set obtained by deleting the last coordinate of each point of $P$. Then for every real number $n$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d + 1) = n \cdot \mathrm{opx}(n, \mathrm{Pr}(P), d)$.
nodes.title: Patterns with a constant last coordinate

nodes.summary: Let $a > 0$, $b$ and $c > 0$ be real numbers and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be strictly increasing on $[0, a]$ with $(f(t) - f(s)) / (t - s) \le b$ whenever $0 \le s < t \le a$. Let $P = \{(t, f(t)) : t \in [0, a]\}$ be the graph of $f$ over $[0, a]$ and, for $k \ge 1$, let $Q_{P,k,c} = \{(x, y, ic) : (x, y) \in P,\ i \in \{1, \dots, k\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then, as the real number $n \to \infty$,…
nodes.title: Stacked graphs of increasing functions in three dimensions

nodes.summary: Let $X_1, \dots, X_d$ be finite sets of real numbers, $k_i = |X_i|$, and $P = X_1 \times \dots \times X_d \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. Put $\alpha = \max_i k_i / \prod_i k_i$ if $d \ge 1$ and every $k_i$ is positive, and $\alpha = 0$ otherwise. Then $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) = O(n^{d - \alpha})$ as the natural number $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Upper bound for higher-dimensional grid patterns

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number and let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be finite. Then the $d$-dimensional continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d)$ and the $d$-dimensional 0-1 matrix extremal function $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P, d)$ of $P$ satisfy $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) = \Theta(\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P, d))$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity, with constants depending on $P$.
nodes.title: Higher-dimensional continuous Turán numbers versus extremal functions

nodes.summary: For every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and all real numbers $m \le n$, $\mathrm{opx}(m, P, d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n, P, d)$.
nodes.title: Higher-dimensional continuous Turán numbers are monotone in the side length

nodes.summary: Let $P, Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. If $Q$ contains $P$, then $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n, Q, d)$ for every real number $n$.
nodes.title: Higher-dimensional continuous Turán numbers are monotone under containment

nodes.summary: For every dimension $d$, real number $n$ and set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Higher-dimensional continuous Turán numbers are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a nonempty open set, and let $Q_P$ be the set of points of $P$ all of whose coordinates are rational. Then, as the real number $n \to \infty$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) = \Theta(n^d)$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_P, d) = \Theta(n^d)$.
nodes.title: Nonempty open patterns in dimension at least two

nodes.summary: For every $d$ there is a real number $C$ such that for every real $c > 0$ there is a real number $K$ with the following property. Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of $k$ points such that, for each coordinate $i$, distinct points of $P$ have distinct $i$-th coordinates and consecutive values of the $i$-th coordinate on $P$ differ by at most $c$. Then…
nodes.title: Upper bound for higher-dimensional permutation-type patterns

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of at least two points with pairwise distinct $x$-coordinates and pairwise distinct $y$-coordinates, and for $i \in \{2, 3\}$ let $P_i = \{(x, y, j) : (x, y) \in P,\ j \in \{1, \dots, i\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then, as $n$ tends to infinity through the natural numbers, $\mathrm{opx}(n, P_2, 3) = \Theta(n^{5/2})$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n, P_3, 3) = \Theta(n^{8/3})$.
nodes.title: Stacked permutation patterns in three dimensions

nodes.summary: Let $r > 0$ and $c > 0$, let $P = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| \le r,\ |y| \le r,\ x = 0 \text{ or } y = 0\}$ be the plus sign of size $r$, and for $t \in \{2, 3\}$ let $Q_{P,t,c} = \{(x, y, ic) : (x, y) \in P,\ i \in \{1, \dots, t\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then, as the real number $n$ tends to infinity, $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P,2,c}, 3) = \Theta(n^{5/2})$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P,3,c}, 3) = \Theta(n^{8/3})$.
nodes.title: Stacked plus signs in three dimensions

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a natural number and let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a nonempty open set. Let $P' = P \times \{0\}^{m+1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{m+3}$, and let $Q_{P'}$ be the set of points of $P'$ all of whose coordinates are rational. Then $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P'}, m + 3) = \Theta(n^{m+3})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Rational points of an embedded open planar set

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$ and $t \ge 2$ be natural numbers and let $c > 0$. For $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ let $Q_{P,t,c} = \{(x, ic) : x \in P,\ i \in \{1, \dots, t\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$. Then there is a real constant $K$, depending only on $d$, $t$ and $c$, such that for every $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and every real $n > 0$,…
nodes.title: Upper bound for continuous Turán numbers of stacked patterns

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contain three points with pairwise distinct $x$-coordinates, and suppose that $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) = O(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity. Let $c > 0$ and $Q_{P,3,c} = \{(x, y, z) : (x, y) \in P,\ z \in \{c, 2c, 3c\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P,3,c}, 3) = \Theta(n^{8/3})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Three-layer stacks of patterns with linear continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ have at least two points, and suppose that $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) = O(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity. Let $c > 0$ and $Q_{P,2,c} = \{(x, y, z) : (x, y) \in P,\ z \in \{c, 2c\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P,2,c}, 3) = \Theta(n^{5/2})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Two-layer stacks of patterns with linear continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a real number $n$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d)$ is the supremum of the $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measures $\mu_d(S)$ over all open sets $S \subseteq [0, n]^d$ that do not contain $P$ in the sense of containment of point sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$; it is $0$ when there is no such set.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number in $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.summary: Let $a, b, n$ be real numbers with $0 < a \le n$ and $0 < b \le n$, and let $P$ be the closed segment from $(0, 0)$ to $(a, b)$. Then the continuous Turán number satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = (a + b)n - ab$.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a diagonal segment

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be finite, and let $c > 0$ and $d$ be real numbers such that any two consecutive distinct $x$-coordinates of points of $P$ differ by at least $c$ and at most $d$, and likewise for $y$-coordinates. Let $q > 1$ and $qP = \{qp : p \in P\}$. Then for every real $n > 0$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, qP) \le (\lceil qd/c \rceil + 1)^2 \, \mathrm{opx}(m, P)$, where…
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a dilated finite pattern

nodes.summary: For every real number $n$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, \emptyset) = 0$: every set contains the empty pattern, so no set avoids it.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of the empty pattern

nodes.summary: Let $s > 0$ and $c > 0$ be real numbers and let $P_{s,2,c} = [0, s] \times \{c, 2c\}$ be the equal-sign pattern, two horizontal segments of length $s$ at heights $c$ and $2c$. Then, as the real number $n$ tends to infinity with $s$ and $c$ fixed, $\operatorname{opx}(n, P_{s,2,c}) = \Theta(s^{1/2} n^{3/2})$.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of the equal-sign pattern

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite sets of real numbers, let $P = X \times Y$ be the grid they span and let $t = |X|$ be its number of columns. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n^{2 - 1/t})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity, where for $t = 0$ (so that $P$ is empty) the exponent $2 - 1/t$ is read as $2$.
nodes.title: Upper bound for the continuous Turán number of a grid

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite sets of real numbers with $|X| = 3$ and $|Y| \ge 3$, and let $P = X \times Y$ be the grid with $3$ columns and $|Y|$ rows. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(n^{5/3})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a grid with three columns

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite sets of real numbers with $|X| = 2$ and $|Y| \ge 2$, and let $P = X \times Y$ be the grid with $2$ columns and $|Y|$ rows. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(n^{3/2})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a grid with two columns

nodes.summary: Let $a, b, c, n$ be real numbers with $0 \le c \le n$, and let $P = [a, a + c] \times \{b\}$ be the closed horizontal segment of length $c$ at height $b$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = cn$.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a horizontal segment

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $a_i \le b_i$ and $y_i$ be real numbers for $i = 1, \dots, k$, such that the intervals $[a_i, b_i]$ are pairwise disjoint and the heights $y_i$ are pairwise distinct, and let $P = \bigcup_{i=1}^k [a_i, b_i] \times \{y_i\}$. Then the continuous Turán number satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Linear bound for separated horizontal segments

nodes.summary: Let $a > 0$ and $b$ be real numbers and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be strictly increasing on $[0, a]$ with $(f(t) - f(s)) / (t - s) \le b$ for all $s < t$ in $[0, a]$. Then the graph $P = \{(t, f(t)) : t \in [0, a]\}$ satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of the graph of an increasing function

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $(x_0, y_0) \in P$ be such that every point of $P$ has $x$-coordinate at most $x_0$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P \cup \{(x_0 + c, y_0)\}) \le \operatorname{opx}(n, P) + cn$ for all real numbers $c > 0$ and $n > 0$.
nodes.title: Adding a point to the right of a pattern

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$. Then the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P)$ and the 0-1 matrix extremal function $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ of $P$ on the $n \times n$ grid satisfy $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) = O(\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P))$ as $n \to \infty$ through the natural numbers.
nodes.title: Upper bound for continuous Turán numbers of finite patterns

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$. Then the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P)$ and the 0-1 matrix extremal function $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ of $P$ on the $n \times n$ grid satisfy $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P))$ as $n \to \infty$ through the natural numbers, with constants depending on $P$.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán numbers versus 0-1 matrix extremal functions

nodes.summary: For every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and all real numbers $m \le n$, the continuous Turán numbers satisfy $\operatorname{opx}(m, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(n, P)$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the continuous Turán number in the side length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a real number and let $P, Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. If $Q$ contains $P$ in the sense of containment of planar point sets, then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(n, Q)$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the continuous Turán number under containment

nodes.summary: For every real number $n$ and every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For every nonempty open set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(n^2)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Open patterns have quadratic continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: There is a real constant $C$ such that for every real $c > 0$ there is a real constant $K$ with the following property. Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of $k$ points whose $x$-coordinates are pairwise distinct and whose $y$-coordinates are pairwise distinct, such that any two consecutive $x$-coordinates of points of $P$ differ by at most $c$, and so do any two consecutive $y$-coordinates. Then…
nodes.title: Linear bound for permutation-like point patterns

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a nonempty open set and let $Q_P$ be the set of points of $P$ both of whose coordinates are rational. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, Q_P) = \Theta(n^2)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Rational points of open patterns have quadratic continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For every real number $n$ and every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the value $\operatorname{opx}(n, P)$ does not change when $P$ is replaced by its image under the rotation by $90^\circ$, $(x, y) \mapsto (-y, x)$, under the reflection $(x, y) \mapsto (-x, y)$, or under the reflection $(x, y) \mapsto (x, -y)$.
nodes.title: Rotation and reflection invariance of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $s, c > 0$ be real numbers, and let $P_{s,t,c} = [0, s] \times \{c, 2c, \dots, tc\}$ be the union of the $t$ horizontal segments of length $s$ at heights $c, 2c, \dots, tc$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P_{s,t,c}) = O(s^{1/t} n^{2 - 1/t})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity, with $s$, $t$ and $c$ fixed.
nodes.title: Upper bound for stacked horizontal segments

nodes.summary: For every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and all real numbers $m, n > 0$, $\operatorname{opx}(m, P) + \operatorname{opx}(n, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(m + n, P)$.
nodes.title: Superadditivity of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a real number, $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ a set and $v \in \mathbb{R}^2$ a vector, and let $P + v = \{p + v : p \in P\}$ be the translate of $P$ by $v$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P + v) = \operatorname{opx}(n, P)$.
nodes.title: Translation invariance of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For each real $n$ let $Q_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set all of whose points have $y$-coordinate $0$ or $1$, whose least $x$-coordinate is $0$ and whose greatest $x$-coordinate is $s(n)$. Then the following are equivalent: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $\operatorname{opx}(n, Q_n) \ge n^{2 - \varepsilon}$ for all sufficiently large real $n$; and for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $s(n) \ge n^{1 - \varepsilon}$ for all…
nodes.title: Two-row patterns of growing width

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and $(x_0, y_0) \in P$ with $x \le x_0$ for every $(x, y) \in P$, and let $c \ge 0$ and $n > 0$ be real numbers. Then
nodes.title: Extending a pattern by a horizontal segment at its right edge

nodes.summary: For a real number $n$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the continuous Turán number $\operatorname{opx}(n, P)$ is the supremum of the Lebesgue measures $\mu_2(S)$ over all open sets $S \subseteq [0, n]^2$ that do not contain $P$ in the sense of point-set pattern containment; it is $0$ when there is no such set.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number in the plane

nodes.summary: For every real number $n$ and every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $\operatorname{osat}(n, P) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: The saturation function is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For every real number $n$ and every point $p \in \mathbb{R}^2$, $\operatorname{osat}(n, \{p\}) = 0$ and $\operatorname{opx}(n, \{p\}) = 0$.
nodes.title: Saturation function and continuous Turán number of a single point

nodes.summary: For a real number $n$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, call an open set $S \subseteq [0, n]^2$ saturating for $P$ if $S$ does not contain $P$ but every open set $S' \subseteq [0, n]^2$ properly containing $S$ contains $P$ (containment in the sense of point-set pattern containment). The saturation function $\operatorname{osat}(n, P)$ is the infimum of the Lebesgue measures $\mu_2(S)$ over all sets $S$…
nodes.title: Saturation function for continuous patterns

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $d$ and $n$, $\operatorname{ex}(n, M_\emptyset, d) = 0$.
nodes.title: The $d$-dimensional extremal function of the empty pattern vanishes

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $d$ and $n$ and every point $p \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $\operatorname{ex}(n, M_{\{p\}}, d) = 0$, since a single point is contained in every nonempty set of cells.
nodes.title: The $d$-dimensional extremal function of a single point vanishes

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $n$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, say that a set $A$ of cells of $\mathbb{N}^d$ contains $P$ when there are maps $f_1, \dots, f_d$ to $\mathbb{N}$, each $f_i$ strictly increasing on the $i$-th coordinates of the points of $P$, with $(f_1(p_1), \dots, f_d(p_d)) \in A$ for every $p \in P$. Then $\operatorname{ex}(n, M_P, d)$ is the largest number of cells of a set of cells of the…
nodes.title: Extremal function of a $d$-dimensional pattern

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, $\operatorname{ex}(n, M_\emptyset) = 0$, since every set of cells contains the empty pattern.
nodes.title: The extremal function of the empty pattern vanishes

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$. For a natural number $n$, write $\mathrm{opx}(n, P)$ for the continuous Turán number of $P$ (the supremum of the Lebesgue measures of the open subsets of $[0, n]^2$ that do not contain $P$, or $0$ if there are none) and $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ for the 0-1 matrix extremal function of $P$ on the $n \times n$ grid. Then $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P) = O(\mathrm{opx}(n, P))$ as…
nodes.title: Lower bound for continuous Turán numbers of finite patterns

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ a set, and let $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ be the largest number of cells of the $n \times n$ grid $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}^2$ forming a set that does not contain $P$ ($0$ if there is no such set). Then $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P) \le n^2$.
nodes.title: Trivial upper bound for the 0-1 matrix extremal function

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every point $p \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the 0-1 matrix extremal function of the one-point pattern $\{p\}$ on the $n \times n$ grid is zero: $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_{\{p\}}) = 0$. Indeed, a single point is contained in every nonempty set of cells.
nodes.title: The extremal function of a single point vanishes

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ is the largest number of cells of the $n \times n$ grid $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}^2$ forming a set that does not contain $P$ (cells contain $P$ when there are strictly increasing maps from the $x$-coordinates of $P$ to columns and from the $y$-coordinates of $P$ to rows that send every point of $P$ to a cell of the set), and $0$ if…
nodes.title: 0-1 matrix extremal function of a point pattern

nodes.summary: Every set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains the empty set $\emptyset$ in the sense of containment of planar point sets.
nodes.title: Every planar set contains the empty pattern

nodes.summary: A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ when there are maps $f_X, f_Y : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f_X(x_0) - f_X(x_1) \ge x_0 - x_1$ whenever $x_0 > x_1$ are $x$-coordinates of points of $P$, $f_Y(y_0) - f_Y(y_1) \ge y_0 - y_1$ whenever $y_0 > y_1$ are $y$-coordinates of points of $P$, and $(f_X(x), f_Y(y)) \in S$ for every $(x, y) \in P$.
nodes.title: Containment of planar point sets

nodes.summary: Let $a, b, c, n$ be real numbers with $c \ge 0$, and let $S \subseteq [0, n]^2$ be an open set that does not contain the closed horizontal segment $[a, a + c] \times \{b\}$ in the sense of containment of planar point sets. Then for every $y \in [0, n]$ the horizontal section $\{x \in \mathbb{R} : (x, y) \in S\}$ has one-dimensional Lebesgue measure at most $c$.
nodes.title: Sections of open sets avoiding a horizontal segment

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a natural number and let $c, n$ be real numbers with $c \ge 0$ and $ct \le n$. Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^t$ be the set of points $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{t-1})$ such that $y_i < n - ic$ for every $i$, $y_{i+1} + c < y_i$ for every $i < t - 1$, and $y_{t-1} > 0$ if $t \ge 1$. Then the $t$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of $X$ is at least $(n/t - c)^t$, where $n/t$ is read as $0$ when $t = 0$.
nodes.title: Lower bound on the volume of a staircase region

conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.
